question.text: A Category III AIF is a pooled investment vehicle that accepts money from:

explanation.text: The Logic: Cat III AIFs pool capital from HNIs and institutional investors due to their high risk/minimum investment requirements. The Trap: Retail investors cannot meet the Rs. 1 crore minimum; foreign-only/government-only are incorrect. Cross-Exam Context: Contrasts with MFs (V-A) that are retail-facing. Distributor's Pro-Tip: Profile investors carefully — many HNIs may still be unsuitable if they need liquidity.
